## Report: Adding Video/Audio to the Timeline

**1. Asset import UI — yes, implemented.**
`apps/studio/src/components/asset-browser/asset-browser-panel.tsx` is the media panel ("Asset Browser"). It has a search box, grid/list toggle, "Unused only" filter, and a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>` triggered by a `+` button (lines 164-181). Selecting files calls `handleImport` (lines 139-151), which reads each file into a `Uint8Array` and calls `kernel.assetEditor.import({ fileName, mimeType, data })`. It's surfaced in the left sidebar via `apps/studio/src/components/rail/left-panel.tsx`, which renders `AssetBrowserPanel` filtered by `AssetType.Video`/`Image`/`Audio` depending on the active rail tab.

**2. Getting onto the Timeline — drag and drop, single unified pipeline.**
Each `AssetTile` in the browser is a `useDraggable` (dnd-kit) with `data: { type: "asset", assetId, assetType, name }` (asset-browser-panel.tsx:54-57). Each `TrackLane` in `apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx` is a `useDroppable` (line 191). One `DndContext` lives at the shell level in `apps/studio/src/components/editor-shell.tsx` (line 189), whose `handleDragEnd` (lines 43-85) distinguishes asset-drops (creates a new clip) from existing-clip drags (repositions). There is no "Add to Timeline" button or auto-add — drag-and-drop is the only path today.

**3. Intent/Command chain.**
- `IAddClipFromAssetIntent` defined in `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/intents.ts:27-37`, constructed in `editor-shell.tsx:56-66`.
- `TimelineEditorService.addClipFromAsset` (`apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/timeline-editor-service.ts:52-78`) resolves it: builds a Layer (`createVideoLayer`/`createImageLayer`/`createAudioLayer` from `@motion-studio/layer`, switched on `assetType` at lines 127-146) and a `TrackItem`, then bundles three Commands into one `CompositeCommand` ("Add clip") and calls `commandBus.execute`:
  - `AddLayerCommand` (`.../commands/add-layer-command.ts`) — adds the layer to the Composition Graph.
  - `AddTrackItemCommand` (`.../commands/add-track-item-command.ts`) — adds the item to `TimelineEngine`.
  - `RegisterAssetReferenceCommand` (`.../commands/register-asset-reference-command.ts`) — records the asset dependency for reference-counting/"unused" filtering.
- Note asset **import** deliberately bypasses the Intent/Command Bus (`AssetEditorService`, `asset-editor-service.ts:4-11` comment) since it's not an undoable "project edit"; only *placing* the asset on the Timeline is a Command/undo-tracked operation.

**4. Status: fully implemented, not stubbed.** No TODO/FIXME/placeholder markers found anywhere in this flow (asset-browser, timeline panel, editor-kernel commands/services). Tests exist for each piece (`add-track-item-command.test.ts`, `add-layer-command.test.ts`, `register-asset-reference-command.test.ts`, `timeline-editor-service.test.ts`, `asset-manager.integration.test.ts`). Undo/redo works via the `CompositeCommand`.

**5. Video vs audio — unified.** One drag-drop pipeline, one Intent, one Service method for all placeable types (Video/Image/Audio); only `createLayerForAsset`'s switch differs by `AssetType`. Font and LUT assets explicitly throw ("cannot be placed on a Timeline") since they aren't track-item-able.</result>

aiTitle: Add video or audio to timeline

content.text:
To add video or audio to the timeline in Motion Studio right now:

1. **Import the file** — In the left sidebar (Asset Browser panel, filtered by Video/Audio tab), click the `+` button to open a file picker. Selected files get read and imported via `kernel.assetEditor.import(...)`.
2. **Drag it onto a track** — Each asset tile in the browser is draggable; each track lane in the Timeline panel is a drop target. Drop the asset tile onto a track lane to create a clip.

There's no "Add to Timeline" button and nothing gets auto-added — **drag-and-drop is currently the only way** to place a clip.

Under the hood, dropping fires `IAddClipFromAssetIntent`, which `TimelineEditorService.addClipFromAsset` resolves into a `CompositeCommand` bundling `AddLayerCommand` + `AddTrackItemCommand` + `RegisterAssetReferenceCommand` — so it's fully undo/redo-able. Video, image, and audio all go through this same unified pipeline (only the Layer factory switches by asset type); fonts/LUTs are explicitly rejected since they can't be track items.

This flow is fully implemented (not a placeholder) — key files: `apps/studio/src/components/asset-browser/asset-browser-panel.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/components/timeline/timeline-panel.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/components/editor-shell.tsx` (drag handling), `apps/studio/src/editor-kernel/services/timeline-editor-service.ts`.

aiTitle: Add video or audio to timeline

content.text:
I found two real bugs, both from missing dnd-kit configuration:

1. **No `DragOverlay`** — the asset tile is only translated via CSS `transform` in place, inside its own `overflow-y-auto` panel. Since the drag preview isn't portaled anywhere, once you drag past the asset panel's bounds it gets clipped and invisible — exactly why nothing shows over the Timeline until you release.
2. **Auto-scroll is on by default** in dnd-kit v6, and it scrolls *every* scrollable ancestor it detects near the pointer — both the Asset Browser's vertical scroll and the Timeline's scroll container. That's the panel-scrolling jank.

Fixing both in `editor-shell.tsx` (add a `DragOverlay` + disable autoScroll) and hiding the source tile while dragging in the two draggable components.

aiTitle: Add video or audio to timeline

content.text:
That matches exactly. Looking at `addTrackItem`, it only has two failure paths: unknown track (won't happen — the trackId always comes from a real rendered track) or **overlap with an existing clip on that track**. Since new clips always get a fixed 3-second default duration wherever you drop them, dropping near or on top of an existing clip on the same track throws:

```
TimelineEngine: track item "<id>" overlaps an existing item on track "<id>".
```

And nothing catches it — `handleDragEnd` calls `commandBus.execute` synchronously with no try/catch, so the exception propagates straight up through the React event handler and crashes the whole app to Next.js's error overlay, for what should just be a rejected drop.

The engine's overlap check itself is correct (it's an intentional invariant per the architecture docs). The bug is that the UI never handles the rejection. Fixing that:
